Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-01-29 15:00 UTC

Topics covered:

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood. Quick check, do we have everyone?
[00:06] Oliver: Yep, Oliver here. Morning our time.
[00:08] Priya: Priya on the call.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:12] Elena: Elena from Redwood, SE. I'll drive the tech bits.

[00:30] Samir: Sweet. The agenda — renewal timing, EU edge onramp, sizing for dedicated pools, and any security questions. Oliver, can you start with where you are on timeline and what you expect from this renewal?
[00:34] Oliver: Sure. So main thing is we are up for renewal end of Feb, we want to lock in capacity for Q2. Our product team is pushing EU-region support — latency matters for EU customers. Right now we're on hosted plan, but the tail latency spikes have been... well, noticeable. So we're evaluating a dedicated pool plus EU edge to keep P95 down.
[01:05] Samir: Got it. When you say "noticeable" can you quantify? p95, p99?
[01:11] Oliver: P95 around 420ms on average during peak, sometimes up to 700ms. p99 occasionally at 1.2s. Traffic is bursty, lots of mid-day spikes. We want P95 < 250ms in EU if possible.
[01:30] Elena: Thanks. That's useful. A Dedicated pool with EU edge nodes usually gets you stable P95s — assuming the model and sequence lengths match our recommended kernel/quantization. Also prefix KV cache helps; but depends how much prompt reuse you have.
[01:50] Priya: We're doing a mix — a lot of short instructions and some long-form summarization, average seq length is ~480 tokens for summaries and 40 tokens for instru- short calls. Means the runtime will have to handle mixed seq distributions.
[02:10] Elena: OK that mixed distribution is fine, we just need to size batchers appropriately. For EU edge we have two options — Hosted EU edge (managed by Redwood) or Private VPC deployment with your VPC peering. Both can achieve low latency; private adds isolation and egress control.
[02:34] Marcus: From procurement: cost delta matters. If dedicated pooled reserved capacity is materially more, we'll need to justify it against SLA improvements. Do you have delta numbers?
[02:45] Samir: We'll send a revised quote. Ballpark — Dedicated reserved reduces per-token variability and can lower p95 but comes with monthly commitment. Burst capacity is available to handle spikes; pricing for burst is higher. I'll put exact numbers in the follow-up.
[02:58] Oliver: Also we need to confirm KMS integration for key management and whether logs are auditable for SOC2. That was a blocker last renewal.
[03:10] Elena: We support KMS integrations — we've done both cloud KMS and HSM-backed setups. There are a couple of patterns depending on whether you choose private control plane or hosted. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS via a secure key-wrapping flow; private on-prem/VPC gives you customer-managed keys but requires ops coordination. Audit logs and key access logs are included in our enterprise package.
[03:40] Priya: Is there latency impact for KMS?
[03:44] Elena: Minimal for normal calls — initial model load / key handshake might add small up-front. For in-flight token encryption we use envelope encryption so per-token cost is negligible. We will share the network diagrams.
[04:00] Samir: For the benchmark, Elena, can you outline what we need from Silvercurrent?
[04:05] Elena: Sure — sample traffic traces (or a representative replay), token distribution (avg/median/p95 seq length), desired SLOs (p50/p95/p99), and any model variants you plan to use. We'll run direct hits vs cached prefixes. We recommend a 4-hour window with peak replay to see autoscaler and batcher behaviour.
[04:32] Oliver: We can provide a day's trace and a smaller spike replay. We'll need instructions for anonymizing customer text. Priya will own preparing that.
[04:40] Priya: Yup, we'll scrub personal data and share synthetic equivalents by next Monday.
[04:46] Elena: Perfect. We'll also need network endpoints whitelisting if you're doing VPC.

[05:10] [fast forward, mid-call, technical deep dive]
[05:12] Elena: On kernel selection and quantization — there might be model variants and some small accuracy regressions if aggressive 4-bit quant is used. For many of your retrieval-augmented tasks, 8-bit or mixed precision gives better tail-latency vs quality tradeoff.
[05:35] Oliver: Hmm, accuracy is important for summaries. We can tolerate a slight drop if latency is solved, but we need to test.
[05:44] Elena: We'll include recommended quantization profiles and a small eval script so you can run quality regressions as part of the benchmark.

[06:10] Marcus: On contract amendments — can you do a 3-month bridge for committed tokens and then a 12-month reserved after we prove EU edge? Procurement likes staged commitments.
[06:20] Samir: Yes we can do a staged offer: a short bridge term then convert to annual reserved with a top-up. We'll draft the contract amendment options.
[06:30] Marcus: Need sample SLA for p95 and credits if missed.
[06:34] Samir: We'll include SLA tables. For Dedicated we can get tighter SLOs.

[07:00] Oliver: Quick question — do you support automated rollbacks to smaller models if latency spikes? We looked at Redwood routing mention in docs but want concrete options.
[07:12] Elena: Yes, routing policies can failover to a cheaper/fast variant automatically. You can define routes by latency, cost, or region. During the benchmark we can simulate a forced failover to validate behavior.

[08:00] [~8 minutes in, clarifying egress and data residency]
[08:05] Priya: Data residency — all user prompts for EU customers must not leave EU. If we go hosted EU edge is that guaranteed?
[08:13] Samir: Hosted EU edge is designed to keep inference and logs in-region; however, metadata in control plane may have to touch Redwood control plane region — we can set up a private control plane variant for stricter residency. We'll detail what remains in-region vs what is control-plane-only.
[08:34] Marcus: Ok need that in writing.

[09:00] Elena: Also note network egress costs. If you're serving heavy embeddings or long responses, egress can be a significant part of bill for EU egress to outside cloud regions. We'll show cost sensitivity.

[10:05] [benchmark logistics discussion]
[10:08] Elena: For the run, best approach: a replay and a synthetic spike. We'll run two modes — cold-start heavy and warm cache. We'll measure P50/P95/P99, throughput, and token cost. Also measure KV cache hit rate.
[10:30] Oliver: For models — we plan to test the open-collection v2 and a tuned summarizer. We'll send model ids (but names may be fuzzy in transcript, sorry if mispronounced).

[12:00] [procurement specific back-and-forth]
[12:05] Marcus: Billing: we need line items for committed tokens, burst pricing, and a separate line for EU-region surcharge. Can you separate Dedicated capacity vs burst usage?
[12:20] Samir: Yes, the quote will show committed capacity (monthly), per-token base rate, burst rates, and a regional uplift if you need dedicated EU capacity. We'll also include a table with example monthly invoices for several traffic profiles.

[15:00] [discussion on security docs and SOC2]
[15:05] Oliver: SOC2 was missing detailed KMS flow last time. We can't move forward without clear KMS integration steps and audit logs described.
[15:15] Elena: We'll attach our SOC2 attestation and a KMS integration guide. For HSM we provide diagrams of key-wrapping flows. There was a past typo in our doc where K-V cache was written as 'KV-cachee' in one place; we'll fix any ambiguity.
[15:35] Priya: Great, also need to know retention windows and possibility to reduce log retention in EU.
[15:42] Elena: Yes retention windows are configurable per-account in enterprise; we will outline defaults and options.

[20:00] [middle: sizing and traffic profile specifics]
[20:10] Elena: Based on your described traffic, I'd recommend a base Dedicated pool sized for your 95th percentile sustained qps with the burst buffer to handle 2x spikes. We can do a cost comparison: smaller pool + higher burst cost vs larger pool + lower burst.
[20:30] Oliver: Let's see concrete numbers. If we target P95 < 250ms, what pool size do we need for 200 qps sustained?
[20:40] Elena: Tentatively, for your model mix, 200 sustained qps needs roughly an X1 pool with 4 GPU nodes (approx). I'll put exact right-sizes after we see the replay. This is approximate because kernels and sequence lengths change the per-gpu throughput.

[25:00] [latency vs quantization tradeoff continued]
[25:10] Elena: Also if you can accept an 8-bit quant profile for the summarizer you might see 20-30% lower token time — we'd advise running accuracy evals.
[25:30] Oliver: Accepted, we'll evaluate with our test set.

[30:00] [wrapping to next steps]
[30:05] Samir: To recap: Redwood sends updated quote (Dedicated + burst, EU uplift), security docs (SOC2, KMS/HSM), a benchmark runbook, and suggested quantization profiles. Silvercurrent provides traffic replay and token distribution and confirms procurement schedule.
[30:30] Marcus: Can we get a draft amendment to the contract with staged 3-month bridge? We want to review before legal weeks of Feb.
[30:38] Samir: Yes, we'll include a bridge option.

[35:00] [Q&A and minor clarifications]
[35:10] Priya: For VPC peering — do you require a static egress IP?
[35:15] Elena: We can do static NAT egress or private link depending on cloud. We'll outline options for AWS/GCP/Azure.

[40:00] [final calibrations]
[40:05] Oliver: Ok, last one — are there failover tests for region outage? We need to ensure EU edge fails over to nearby region without exposing EU user data.
[40:20] Elena: You can define failover policy to route EU traffic to a nearby EU-compatible region; if you require strict residency then we recommend private control plane with no cross-border replication. We'll detail the tradeoffs in a matrix.

[48:00] [closing minutes]
[48:05] Samir: Great, we'll follow up with the items. Anything else?
[48:12] Marcus: No, thanks.
[48:14] Oliver: Nope, thanks folks.
[48:16] Priya: Thanks.
[48:20] Elena: Thanks everyone. We'll set up the benchmark time via email.
[48:25] Samir: I'll send the pricing + docs by Wednesday.

[52:00] End of recording.
